data.name: Farzand
data.gender_notes: Farzand is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who aspires to be a ruler or a leader, a prince, an heir. The name Farzand carries the meaning “Prince, Heir” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Urdu. Parents who choose Farzand usually hope their child will grow to embody prince, heir and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A soul destined for greatness and leadership, a future leader or a warrior.
data.etymology: Farzand belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Prince, Heir.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farzand total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: فرزند
in_arabic.long_meaning: الفرزند كلمة عربية بمعنى الابن أو الولد، وتُستخدم بشكل شائع للإشارة إلى طفل أو شاب. تُشتق الكلمة من الفعل "فَرز"، والذي يعني "أن يُولد" أو "أن يُسْرَى". ويُمكن العثور على هذا الفعل في الآيات القرآنية والحديث النبوي. وتُشير إلى هوية الشخص كابن لوالديه، وتُعبّر عن ربطه بالأسرة وسبق الأجيال. تُعتبر كلمة "فرزند" من الأسماء الشائعة في العالم العربي والإسلامي.

in_urdu.name: فرزند
in_urdu.long_meaning: فرزند ایک عربی الفاظ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے بیٹا یا اولاد۔ عام طور پر یہ لفظ بچے یا نوجوان کو ظاہر کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ یہ لفظ عربی فعل "فَرز" سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے "پیدا ہونا" یا "پیدا ہونے والا"۔ یہ فعل قرآن و حدیث میں بھی ملتا ہے۔ یہ لفظ کسی شخص کی والدین سے وابستگی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے اور اس کی خاندانی اور نسلی شناخت کو دکھاتا ہے۔ فرزند ایک مشہور نام ہے جو مسلم دنیا میں بکثرت استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: फ़रज़ांद
in_hindi.long_meaning: फ़रज़ांद एक अरबी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ है बेटा या वंशज। यह शब्द आमतौर पर बच्चे या युवा को संदर्भित करने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है। यह शब्द अरबी क्रिया "فَرز" से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है "जन्म लेना" या "पैदा होना"। यह क्रिया कुरान और हदीस में भी मिलती है। यह शब्द किसी व्यक्ति के माता-पिता से संबंध को दर्शाता है और उसका पारिवारिक और वंशानुगत महत्व को व्यक्त करता है। फ़रज़ांद एक लोकप्रिय नाम है जो भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: فرزند
in_pashto.long_meaning: فرزند پښتو ژبه کې دې ته د ولې، لکړې، نوړې هم په نوم یادونه کېږي. د لفظ په معنا کې د لکو دې خاندان ته یا ژوندې ته د وړانديز په ګڼه معنا لري. د لفظ د منشاء په اړه د عربي ژبې څخه راغلي او په عرب وخت کې د لکو دې خاندان ته د دې یې اړوندیت په معنا کې د استعمال یې شروعه شوې ده. په افغانستان کې دا نوم په ګڼه کيږي او د خاندان ته د لکو دې د ورځي په معنا کې د استعمال یې شروعه شوې ده.

in_english.name: Farzand
in_english.long_meaning: Farzand is an Arabic name meaning 'son' or 'offspring'. Derived from the root 'Faraza,' which signifies 'to give birth' or 'to create,' it evokes a sense of lineage, family connection, and the continuation of generations. Commonly used in Islamic cultures, Farzand carries connotations of respect, responsibility, and the inherent value of each individual within the family structure. It is a name often bestowed upon boys, signifying their role as heirs and future leaders within their communities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Farzand holds a strong cultural significance in the Persian and Muslim world. The term 'Farzand' translates to pronoun works as a title of respect and honor, equivalent to the English titles 'Lord' or 'Sir'. It is used to acknowledge the nobility or aristocracy in an individual. Historically, the title was bestowed upon the heirs of rulers and leaders, signifying their future role as leaders and successors. Today, the name is popular among the Muslim populations in the Indian subcontinent and Persian-speaking countries as a given name, symbolizing the desire for lineage, legacy, and leadership.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Farzand has its roots in the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), who emphasized that every person is born as a ruler (Amir) of their soul. This concept is widely known as being the 'Caliph of Your Own Self.' The name carries the potential meaning of 'ruler over one's self,' suggesting self-control, discipline, and the pursuit of spiritual growth. In this regard, those who bear the name Farzand are called to aspire to truly fulfill their role as the 'ruler of their own selves,' a title bestowed upon them by their Creator, leading to a life of spiritual enrichment anddhikr (remembrance of God).
data.spiritual_symbolism: Farzand is an Arabic term meaning "offspring" or "son." It is a name filled with pride and love, symbolizing the precious bond between a parent and their child, a reflection of God's infinite mercy and creation.

historical_references.reference: The Mughal prince Dara Shikoh, who was the eldest son of Emperor Shah Jahan, was given the title 'Farzand-i-Ilahi' or 'Divine Heir'. This title was bestowed upon him by his father Shah Jahan in 1623 when Dara was around 7-8 years old.
historical_references.context: Dara Shikoh was seen as the chosen successor of his father, Shah Jahan, and was given the title 'Farzand-i-Ilahi' or 'Divine Heir' to reflect his divine status and rightful claim to the throne.

historical_references.reference: Another historical figure who was given the name 'Farzand' was Mirza Ghulam Ahmed, the founder of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in 1889. The name 'Farzand-i-Khudda' or 'Chosen of God' was given to him by his mentor and spiritual guide, Maulvi Qasim Nanautawi.
historical_references.context: Mirza Ghulam Ahmed was seen as a messiah figure, and the title 'Farzand-i-Khudda' or 'Chosen of God' was given to him to reflect his divine status and role as a leader of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name 'Farzand' which means 'offspring' or 'heir' is increasingly used in modern contexts. In urbanized societies, it is used to denote the next generation of a family or community, especially in the context of preserving and passing on cultural and religious traditions. In the era of globalization, Farzand is also used to refer to the younger generation of Muslims around the world who are working to bridge cultural gaps and promote unity and solidarity. With technological advancements, Farzand is seen in various digital platforms. For instance, on social media, it is used as a hashtag to refer to the younger generation of Muslims and their contributions to society. In education, it is used in the context of schools and institutions that focus on preserving and promoting Islamic heritage and values for the next generation. In business, it is used in companies and organizations that cater to the needs of the younger Muslim population, such as digital marketing agencies and Islamic finance institutions.
